subject: Crash using multicore and glm with parallel = TRUE

messages.author: cf98ec64431c34d5
messages.subject: Crash using multicore and glm with parallel = TRUE
parts:
I am running OS X Lion, playing with some timing stuff to to see
effect of multiple cores, and found that calling glm with .parallel =
TRUE causes a segfault. Essentially the same line of code that only
calls a lm() instead of glm() runs fine..

Should I send this elsewhere? Not sure if this is really a plyr problem.

Eric

*** caught segfault ***
address 0x108, cause 'memory not mapped'

*** caught segfault ***
address 0x108, cause 'memory not mapped'

*** caught segfault ***
address 0x108, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
1: drop(x %*% start)
2: glm.fit(x = c(1, 1, 1, [etc]

R version 2.13.1 (2011-07-08)
Copyright (C) 2011 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
ISBN 3-900051-07-0
Platform: i386-apple-darwin9.8.0/i386 (32-bit)

Code that produces segfault:

library ( foreach)
library ( multicore)
library ( doMC)
library ( plyr)
library ( robust)
ls()

registerDoMC(cores = 6)

# A set of random-junk data

trials <- 18000
abc.df <- data.frame ( a = rnorm ( trials ), b = rnorm ( trials ),
c = rnorm ( trials ) , d = rnorm ( trials) )
# Add a Group variable
abc.df <- transform ( abc.df, G = sample (1:18, size = trials ,
replace = TRUE ), z = sample ( 0:1, size = trials, replace = TRUE) ,
e = exp ( a + b ))

lmfun <- function ( x ) {
for ( i in 1:100 ) lmZ <- lm ( z ~a + b + c + d + e , data = x )
return ( lmZ ) # Keep the last one only... not really doing anything
}

glmfun <- function ( x ) {
for ( i in 1:100 ) glmZ <- glm ( z ~a + b + c + d + e , data = x ,
family = binomial() )
return ( glmZ ) # Keep the last one only... not really doing anything
}

p1time <- system.time ( res1P <- dlply ( .(G), .data = abc.df, .fun =
lmfun , .parallel = FALSE ) )

print ( length ( res1P) )
print ( p1time)


p1gtime <- system.time ( res1Pg <- dlply ( .(G), .data = abc.df, .fun
= glmfun , .parallel = FALSE ) )

print ( length ( res1Pg) )
print ( p1gtime)

p6time <- system.time ( res6P <- dlply ( .(G), .data = abc.df, .fun =
lmfun , .parallel = TRUE ) )

print ( length ( res6P) )
print ( p6time)

# This line segfaults:
p6gtime <- system.time ( res6Pg <- dlply ( .(G), .data = abc.df, .fun
= glmfun , .parallel = TRUE ) )

print ( length ( res6Pg) )
print ( p6gtime)
